A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AniMer and CtrlAni3D and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative animal reconstruction experiments, including dataset, backbone, contrastive-loss, and training-stage ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds transfer, decoder, and species-level analyses in supplementary Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: Equation (1) revises the stated contrastive objective by dividing similarities by a positive temperature parameter tau in both numerator and denominator. The architecture, direct SMAL regression, two-stage training, and other losses remain unchanged. An implementation change or experimental rerun is not established.

E1.justification: The training datasets and evaluation coverage remain the same. New transfer experiments and species breakdowns reuse existing datasets and animal populations. Generative Zoo is discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds an MLP-decoder comparator, AniMer-e, in Table 9 and a classification-loss comparator in Table 10. HMR2.0's quantitative results move from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 1; they are not a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated annotation coverage to include Zebra Synthetic among datasets with 3D labels; actual changes to its use in training are not established. New protocols include training exclusively on Animal3D or CtrlAni3D. Existing metrics, validation ratio, and 500/700-epoch training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analyses: CtrlAni3D's contribution to 3D accuracy, synthetic-to-real transfer, an MLP-decoder ablation, and species-level classification-versus-contrastive comparisons appear in Tables 7–10. Figure 9 adds Animal3D annotation and model-fitting failure examples. Earlier training-stage and qualitative failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance procedures. v2's performance ranges across different hyperparameters and devices describe setting sensitivity, without introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 7–10 add substantial new results on transfer, component choice, and species-level behavior. For example, Table 7 reports Animal3D PA-MPJPE of 82.6 without CtrlAni3D and 80.4 with it. Existing main-table values and the relocated HMR2.0 and training-stage results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1) gains temperature scaling and explicitly defines tau as positive, changing the mathematical definition of the contrastive loss. The SMAL and camera definitions and remaining loss equations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: family-aware Transformer reconstruction, the CtrlAni3D synthesis pipeline, aggregated training data, and improved reconstruction and generalization. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of the synthetic-to-real domain gap, Animal3D fitting errors, and why contrastive learning may help geometry and rare species more than classification. It also qualifies the training-stage interpretation: one-stage training might achieve comparable results with additional steps or tuning, beyond v1's emphasis on superiority at equal budgets.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports one week of training on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and explains ambiguous-species prompt selection and SAM2-dependent background selection. Conversely, v1's explicit appendix description of the adapted, two-stage HMR2.0 control is omitted. The project-page address remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds 3D-LFM, DeepLabCut, SLEAP, and SuperAnimal when distinguishing keypoint methods from surface reconstruction, plus Generative Zoo in future work. The central positioning relative to SMAL, HMR2.0, and diffusion-based synthesis remains stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained, with localized related-work and experimental-summary rewrites. The supplement is reorganized from Sections A–D into A–F, separating dataset comparison, additional analyses, qualitative results, and failures. Affiliation and acknowledgement text also changes.

P2.justification: Result presentation expands with four new analysis tables and the Animal3D failure-case figure. Figure 4 gains an HMR2.0 column and removes one example; existing HMR2.0 scores move into Table 1. Appendix displays are redistributed, while most original figures and their content are retained.

improvement.justification: The new transfer and classification-versus-contrastive analyses strengthen evidence for the existing contributions, while training-cost disclosure and the qualified two-stage interpretation improve transparency. The gain is moderated by reduced detail about the HMR2.0 control and an introduced labeling conflict: Table 9 calls the ResNet variant AniMer-b, whereas Section 5.2 uses that name for the variant without pretraining.
